name: MonarchAiStructuredAnswer
title: AiStructuredAnswer
wrapsNative: VStack of LabeledContent with MonarchLabeledContentStyle, Grid with GridRow and gridCellColumns for the grid layout, MonarchBadge in MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge and redacted(reason: .placeholder)
summary: A model's structured output shown as labelled fields (text, lists, numbers, badges or Markdown) instead of prose, filling in as it streams with placeholders for the fields still to come.
whenToUse: When the model returns structured data that follows a schema, such as an interview brief, a lead summary or fields extracted from a document, and people compare such answers.
whenNotToUse: For free-form answers use MonarchAiMarkdown or MonarchAiStreamingText. For many rows of the same shape use MonarchAiTableAnswer. For facts the app already knows, not generated, use LabeledContent with the Monarch style.
api: init(_ schema: [MonarchAiStructuredField], data: [String: MonarchAiJSON], title: String? = nil, layout: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout = .list, isStreaming: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels = MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels(), onOpenLink: (@MainActor (URL) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)
init(_ schema:, data:, title:, layout:, isStreaming:, labels:, onOpenLink:)  // Actions == EmptyView

struct MonarchAiStructuredField { init(_ key: String, label: String, type: MonarchAiStructuredFieldType = .text, format: MonarchMetricFormat = .number, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, toneForValue: (@Sendable (String) -> MonarchTone)? = nil, isWide: Bool? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiStructuredFieldType { case text, list, number, badge, markdown }
struct MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels { init(aiAnswer: String? = nil, pending: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, complete: String? = nil) }

options.name: schema
options.description: The fields in order: key, label, type, number format, badge tone and width. Values whose key is not in the schema are ignored.

options.name: data
options.description: The values by key, usually parsed from the model's structured output. Treated as untrusted.

options.name: title
options.description: A title under the AI answer label, such as Interview brief.

options.name: layout
options.description: .list: one field per row, the label beside a short value and above a long one. .grid: each field as a small card, two to a row, one to a row at accessibility text sizes; wide fields span the row.

options.name: isStreaming
options.description: The answer is still arriving: missing fields show placeholders read as Still generating.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces AI answer, Still generating, Not provided and Response complete.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links of Markdown fields in the app.

options.name: actions
options.description: Views after the fields, such as a copy button or feedback buttons; they wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.type
options.description: text: plain text. list: an array as a bulleted list. number: written with format in the reader's locale. badge: one MonarchBadge per value. markdown: rendered by MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.format
options.description: How a number field is written: a number, a percentage of a ratio or a currency, as MonarchMetric writes it.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.tone / toneForValue
options.description: The tone of a badge field's badges, fixed or from each value.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.isWide
options.description: Spans the full width; nil makes list and markdown fields wide.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every field shows its value; a field without one shows a dash read as Not provided.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Fields that have not arrived show a static placeholder bar read as Still generating, so the layout does not jump as they arrive.

appearance: A card on the surface role with the default border and a large radius. The AI answer label is MonarchAiGeneratedBadge in the AI roles; the title is strong body text. Labels are muted captions, values default body text, empty values a dash in the subtle role, bullets muted. In the grid layout each field is a card on the subtle background with a subtle border. Every role follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds on DescriptionList; iOS uses LabeledContent with MonarchLabeledContentStyle, the iOS description list. The web's Intl.NumberFormat options become MonarchMetricFormat (number, percent, currency), the format MonarchMetric uses; numeric text such as 1,200 is read as a number and text ending in % stays as written. The web's grid layout uses responsive auto columns; on iPhone it is a SwiftUI Grid of two columns, one at accessibility text sizes. The web's shimmer placeholder is a static redacted placeholder here, so there is nothing to stop for Reduce Motion. The web's headingLevel and locale props are not offered: VoiceOver gives the title the header trait, and the locale comes from the environment. Values are MonarchAiJSON, the conversation model's JSON type. Android has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The AI answer label and the title are one element with the header trait, so the provenance is spoken with the title.
Each field is one element read as its label and then its value; list and badge items are read separated by commas.
A field still to come is read as Still generating, and an empty one as Not provided, not as a dash.
A Markdown field keeps its own elements, so its headings and links stay reachable.
Response complete. is announced once when streaming ends, never per field.
Badges carry their value as text, so their tone is never the only signal.
edgeCases: HTML in a value is shown as text; Markdown fields go through MonarchAiMarkdown, which never renders HTML.
Empty text, null and empty arrays count as missing; a single value in a list field is a one-item list.
Objects and arrays in a text field are shown as compact JSON.
An odd number of narrow fields in the grid leaves the last row half filled.
Long values wrap; nothing scrolls sideways.

examples.title: Interview brief
examples.template:
MonarchAiStructuredAnswer(
    [
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.0.key}}, label: {{schema.0.label}}, type: {{schema.0.type|case}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.1.key}}, label: {{schema.1.label}}, type: {{schema.1.type|case}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.2.key}}, label: {{schema.2.label}}, type: {{schema.2.type|case}}, tone: {{schema.2.tone|tone}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.3.key}}, label: {{schema.3.label}}, type: {{schema.3.type|case}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.4.key}}, label: {{schema.4.label}}, type: {{schema.4.type|case}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.5.key}}, label: {{schema.5.label}}, type: {{schema.5.type|case}}),
        MonarchAiStructuredField({{schema.6.key}}, label: {{schema.6.label}}, type: {{schema.6.type|case}}),
    ],
    data: [
        {{schema.0.key}}: {{brief.candidate}},
        {{schema.1.key}}: {{brief.role}},
        {{schema.2.key}}: {{brief.stage}},
        {{schema.3.key}}: {{brief.score}},
        {{schema.4.key}}: [{{brief.strengths.0}}, {{brief.strengths.1}}],
        {{schema.5.key}}: [{{brief.risks.0}}],
        {{schema.6.key}}: {{brief.summary}},
    ],
    title: {{title}}
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiStructuredAnswer(
    [
        MonarchAiStructuredField("candidate", label: "Candidate", type: .text),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("role", label: "Role", type: .text),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("stage", label: "Stage", type: .badge, tone: .info),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("score", label: "Overall score", type: .number),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("strengths", label: "Strengths", type: .list),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("risks", label: "Open questions", type: .list),
        MonarchAiStructuredField("summary", label: "Summary", type: .markdown),
    ],
    data: [
        "candidate": "Alex Morgan",
        "role": "Senior engineer",
        "stage": "Final interview",
        "score": 4.2,
        "strengths": ["Clear system design reasoning", "Strong written communication"],
        "risks": ["Limited on-call experience"],
        "summary": "Interviewers agree on **technical depth**. Confirm availability for the start date.",
    ],
    title: "Interview brief"
)
